hints: Notice from the diagram that X starts 50 m behind Y, with constant velocities $30 \text{m s}^{-1}$ and $20 \text{m s}^{-1}$ in the same direction.
Think about relative motion: because both move forward, X only gains on Y at the difference $30 - 20 = 10 \text{m s}^{-1}$.
Divide the initial 50 m gap by that closing speed to find the time when their displacements from the start become equal.
walkthrough: Take the starting position of X as zero, so at time $t$ its displacement is $s_X = v_X t$ and Y starts 50 m ahead so $s_Y = 50 + v_Y t$, with distances in $\text{m}$.
For constant velocity use $s = vt$, giving $s_X = 30t$ and $s_Y = 50 + 20t$.
X is level with Y when $s_X = s_Y$, so $30t = 50 + 20t$.
Rearrange to $(30-20)t = 50$, so $10t = 50$ and $t = 5.0 \text{s}$, with units of $\text{m}$ divided by $\text{m s}^{-1}$ giving $\text{s}$.
